name: Majority Completion Bounds Ordering Width
statement: If the one-inclusion graph of $C$ is connected, then $\operatorname{med}(C)$ is an isometric median superclass of width zero, $\sigma(C)\leq\delta_{\mathrm{med}}(C)$, and the defect is the minimum number of additions needed for an isometric median superclass. On partial cubes it vanishes exactly on median graphs.
proof: Majority closure preserves connectedness. Ordering its concepts by distance from a chosen root gives only singleton minimal predecessor disagreements, so it is isometric, median, and width zero. Deletion stability gives the inequality; every median superclass must contain all iterated coordinatewise majorities.
